sources.name: North_America.pdf
sources.text:
NORTH AMERICA / ABOUT THIS VOLUME
A continent in many voices
North America reaches from Arctic communities to the tropical
isthmus and the islands of the Caribbean.
This book uses a broad geographic definition of North America: Canada and the United States,
Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean. It gives each of the region’s 23 sovereign countries
its own chapter. Greenland, Puerto Rico and other non-sovereign places appear in a separate
reference section.
Start with a place
A country opener gives a photograph, then a flag, population figure and identity panel. Maps
locate neighbours, major towns, administrative divisions and selected physical features. The
following pages explain history, government, livelihoods and culture.
Names should be usable
Crowded division maps use numbers tied to a full-name key. Capitals and local centres appear
in tables. An island, a province and a country are different things; the text makes those
distinctions wherever they matter.
Numbers have dates
Population estimates describe a particular year. They may differ from a national census,
especially where migration is rapid or counting is difficult. The source and year accompany each
figure. Political descriptions use a reference date of 11 October 2026.
India’s outline throughout
Every world locator in this edition uses official Survey of India international-boundary data. The
world-reference appendix uses the same outline. This depicts India’s official territorial position;
it does not settle international boundary disputes.
Reading a country fairly
A chapter can introduce a country without speaking for every resident. Indigenous and
Afro-descendant histories, migration and regional differences belong beside national events.

A shared island
Saint Martin and Sint Maarten share an island. The northern part is a French overseas
collectivity; the southern part is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
A geographic choice
This volume follows the broad North American scope of the UN M49 grouping: Northern
America, Central America and the Caribbean. Territories are included as geographic places, with
their status explained.
Status sources: UN M49 regions · U.S. Office of Insular Affairs · Kingdom of the Netherlands · British Overseas
Territories. Reference date: 11 October 2026.

NORTH AMERICA / REGIONAL OVERVIEW
The Caribbean’s 13 sovereign states
Some countries occupy one main island. Others include part of a larger
island or a chain of smaller ones.
Cuba
Haiti Dominican
Republic Jamaica
Bahamas

Barbuda

and Nevis Dominica

Saint Vincent and
the Grenadines
Grenada
Trinidad and
Tobago
Shared waters, different states
Haiti and the Dominican Republic share Hispaniola. Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and
Grenada divide the Grenadine island chain between them. The Bahamas lies in the Atlantic,
north of the main Antillean arc.
Countries and other places
Puerto Rico, Martinique, Guadeloupe and several other islands are not sovereign states. Their
separate constitutional arrangements appear in Appendix B. The overview highlights the 13
sovereign states in green.

APPENDIX B / NON-SOVEREIGN PLACES
North America beyond its sovereign states
These places belong in a geographic portrait of the region. Their legal
arrangements differ, so they are not counted among the 23 sovereign
countries.
Anguilla
United Kingdom · The Valley
British Overseas Territory north of Saint Martin.
Cayman Islands
United Kingdom · George Town
British Overseas Territory comprising Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac and Little Cayman.
Montserrat
United Kingdom · Brades / Plymouth
British Overseas Territory. Plymouth is the historic capital; government operates in the north
after volcanic destruction.
Turks and Caicos Islands
United Kingdom · Cockburn Town
British Overseas Territory; Providenciales is a major population and visitor centre.
Aruba
Kingdom of the Netherlands · Oranjestad
Constituent country within the Kingdom, with its own government; not an independent
sovereign state.
Curaçao
Kingdom of the Netherlands · Willemstad
Constituent country within the Kingdom.

APPENDIX B / NON-SOVEREIGN PLACES
North America beyond its sovereign states
These places belong in a geographic portrait of the region. Their legal
arrangements differ, so they are not counted among the 23 sovereign
countries.
Greenland
Kingdom of Denmark · Nuuk
Self-governing territory; Arctic island and homeland of Inuit communities. It is geographically
North American.
Bermuda
United Kingdom · Hamilton
British Overseas Territory in the Atlantic, far north of the Caribbean island chain.
Saint Pierre and Miquelon
France · Saint-Pierre
French overseas collectivity near Newfoundland.
Puerto Rico
United States · San Juan
U.S. territory with its own elected government; not a U.S. state or an independent country.
U.S. Virgin Islands
United States · Charlotte Amalie
U.S. territory including Saint Thomas, Saint John and Saint Croix.
British Virgin Islands
United Kingdom · Road Town
British Overseas Territory; Tortola is the main population centre.
Status references: Greenland and Denmark · Puerto Rico.
